intro.en: Three rules explain almost every written accent in Spanish.

él.nota: Él with an accent is he. El without one is the.

sí.nota: Sí is yes. Si is if.

té.nota: Té is tea. Te is the pronoun.

texto.en:
Spanish spelling tells you the stress.

1. A word ending in a **vowel, n or s** is stressed on the second-to-last syllable: **ca**sa, **ha**blan, **lu**nes.

2. A word ending in **any other consonant** is stressed on the last syllable: ha**blar**, ciu**dad**, re**loj**.

3. A **tilde** marks every word that breaks rules 1 and 2: ca**fé**, tam**bién**, in**glés**; **ár**bol, **fá**cil, **lá**piz.

4. A word stressed on the third-to-last syllable **always** has a tilde: **mé**dico, te**lé**fono, **dí**melo.

A stressed **i** or **u** next to a, e, o takes a tilde to stand on its own: pa**ís**, d**í**a, r**í**o.

A tilde also separates pairs of short words (see the table), and marks question words, even inside a sentence: no sé **dónde** vive.

Plurals can gain or lose it: joven → **jó**venes; inglés → ingleses; examen → e**xá**menes.

filas: it ends in a vowel, n or s
it does not end in a vowel, n or s

frases.es: Él toma té y yo te espero aquí.
frases.en: He has tea and I wait for you here.

frases.es: Sí, voy si tú vienes con tu hermano.
frases.en: Yes, I'll go if you come with your brother.

frases.es: No sé si se ha ido.
frases.en: I don't know whether he has left.
When are you coming back? When I finish work.

It is stressed on the last syllable and.en: That breaks rule 1, so it is marked.

It is a foreign word.en: The tilde depends on stress, not on origin.

All words ending in -e have one.en: Most do not: coche, madre, calle.

bloques.correcta: It is stressed on the last syllable and ends in a vowel

pregunta.en: Which of these words is missing its tilde?

arbol.en: Árbol: stressed on ár and ending in l, so it breaks rule 2.

Él.en: The pronoun he takes a tilde.

El.en: El without a tilde is the article.

pregunta.en: Complete: I don't know where she lives.

dónde.en: A question word keeps its tilde inside a sentence.

donde.en: Without a tilde it is a relative: la casa donde vive.

exámenes.en: The stress stays on a, which is now third from the end.

examenes.en: The stress would move. The tilde keeps it on a.

examens.en: A noun ending in a consonant adds -es.

texto.en:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (150–180 words).** Write a paragraph of your own and mark every written accent, then explain in writing why five of them are there.

**Speak (about 3 minutes).** Read a text aloud, marking the stress clearly, and explain three pairs such as el and él, si and sí, aun and aún.
